what_its_for: Deutetrabenazine is used to treat two conditions: (1) involuntary, uncontrolled movements (called chorea) caused by Huntington's disease, and (2) uncontrolled, repetitive movements or sounds (called tardive dyskinesia) that can happen as a side effect of certain psychiatric medications. It works by reducing the amount of certain chemicals in the brain that cause these unwanted movements.
how_to_take: Take deutetrabenazine by mouth with food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. If you are taking the twice-daily tablet (Austedo), take one dose in the morning and one in the evening. If you are taking the once-daily extended-release tablet (Austedo XR), take it once a day.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks until your movements are well controlled or until you reach the right dose for you. The starting dose is usually 6 mg per day. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on how well it works and how you tolerate it. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first. The maximum dose depends on your individual situation and whether you take certain other medications.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store deutetrabenazine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may worsen depression. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, as it can cause sleepiness and slow your reaction time. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially antidepressants (MAO inhibitors), other drugs for movement disorders, or medications that affect heart rhythm, as serious interactions can occur. Avoid stopping this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, new or worsening depression or anxiety, severe restlessness or inability to sit still (akathisia), high fever with stiff muscles and confusion (signs of a rare but serious condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome), irregular or fast heartbeat, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing. Also let your doctor know if you feel unusually drowsy, dizzy, or have trouble swallowing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your uncontrolled movements within a few weeks of starting this medication, but it may take several weeks of dose adjustments to get the full benefit. Do not stop taking it even if you do not notice immediate improvement — work with your doctor to find the right dose for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if this medication is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medication. Children: This medication has not been studied in children and is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, especially drowsiness and falls. Use with caution. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or avoid this medication entirely, as it is processed by the liver. Depression or mental health history: Tell your doctor if you have a history of depression, suicidal thoughts, or other mental health conditions, as this medication can worsen these conditions.
